question: An older family album labels a trip “Queen Charlotte Islands,” but a current host writes “Haida Gwaii.” Am I necessarily looking at two different destinations?
generated_answer:
No, you're not looking at two different destinations. "Queen Charlotte Islands" and "Haida Gwaii" refer to the same archipelago located off the coast of British Columbia, Canada. The name change occurred in 2010, when the British Columbia government officially changed the name to Haida Gwaii, which is the name used by the indigenous Haida people to refer to their traditional territory.

The name "Queen Charlotte Islands" was given to the islands by European explorers in the 18th century, in honor of Queen Charlotte, the wife of King George III. However, the Haida people have always known the islands as Haida Gwaii, which means "Islands of the People" in the Haida language.

So, if your family album labels a trip "Queen Charlotte Islands" and a current host writes "Haida Gwaii", it's likely referring to the same destination, just with a different name.
